pull.title: feat(docs): a Docs page in the dashboard, and the Guide brought to 5.48.0
pull.body:
Two related pieces: a **Docs page** that renders the project's own documentation inside the admin UI, and the **Guide** brought from 5.41.1 to 5.48.0. ## Bundled, not fetched The six user-facing documents ship **inside the wheel** rather than being fetched from GitHub, so the page works with no internet and shows the docs for the version actually running — a user on 5.40 shouldn't be reading 5.48's instructions. Each carries a **View on GitHub** link for the latest. Bundling is the part that fails invisibly, so it's proven twice — a real build, and a test that builds a wheel in CI: ``` 7308 my_claude_code/docs_bundle/ANTHROPIC-SUBSCRIPTION.md 93376 my_claude_code/docs_bundle/ARCHITECTURE.md 234320 my_claude_code/docs_bundle/CLAUDE-CODE-CONFIG.md 2634 my_claude_code/docs_bundle/CONTRIBUTING.md 87182 my_claude_code/docs_bundle/README.md 55059 my_claude_code/docs_bundle/USAGE.md ``` A doc missing from the wheel is a page that's empty for every installed user while working perfectly from a source checkout. Slugs are matched against a cached frozenset of files that exist and **never joined onto a path** — traversal impossible by construction, the same shape as the bundled screenshots. Both routes loopback-guarded. Rendering is `markdown-it-py` (already a dependency via `messaging/rendering/`) with **`html: False`**, exactly as the two existing renderers. ## The escaping fix, and what only a browser found Escaping raw HTML is right for safety and wrong for *display*: the README opens with a centred `
` banner that would render as five lines of `<div>`. Lines that are nothing but tags are dropped **before** parsing, so nothing is ever promoted from text to markup. Two cases that rule got wrong, **both found by opening the page, not by a test**: - **Image captions are `

…

`** — tags wrapped around prose, so *not* HTML-only. They survived, got escaped, and put literal markup above the fold. A line that both opens with a tag and closes with one is now unwrapped to its text. - **`` is an autolink, not a tag** — but it opens with a letter, so the HTML-only rule matched the whole line and the URL vanished with no trace. No curated doc has one today; a future one would have lost content silently. Verified through the live API after the fix: **0 literal `<p>`, 0 literal `<em>`**, caption text present. ## Guide → 5.48.0 Context-length failure kind and `FALLBACK_SKIP_KINDS` under models; a new Token Optimizer section (locally-answered requests, the bounded candidates scan, trimming with its measured table); the analytics note that a provider column can read `answered locally · `; corrected Limits text now trimming moved off it; the context-window 400 message under troubleshooting; and the closing pointer now aims at the **Docs** tab rather than a path in the repo. Trimming is presented as **off and not recommended**, numbers read from `.env.example` and the module docstring. ## Three corrections to my brief — two mean I was wrong - **The RTK "Token optimizer" card has NOT moved off Providers.** I told it that text was stale; the Guide was already correct. It verified rather than "fixing" it. - **`answered locally · ` is the display label; the filter *value* is `local:`.** I'd conflated them. - The three env vars removed in 5.44.0 have **zero** stale mentions anywhere, and `known_views` needed no edit because it only constrains onboarding *step targets*. ## Verification **17 mutations, each asserted applied, whole file per run, no `-k`, all CAUGHT** — traversal, `html: False`, both loopback guards, wheel bundling, view registration, and the null-container guard whose absence kills *every* view rather than one. **The matrix caught two things the mutations didn't:** a loopback guard that had gone missing from the single-document route in the working tree (restored, and I re-verified both guards are present myself), and a test asserting `"onclick" not in html` — which **fails on correct output**, because `onclick` survives as literal text inside escaped brackets. **jsdom** vs unmodified `main`: identical section counts for all ten pre-existing views, plus `docs`. **Real browser** — what found the caption bug: ``` pageScrollsHorizontally: false overflowing elements outside a scroll box: 0 scriptTagsInsideDocs: 0 headings 55 · code blocks 39 · tables 19 ``` **Full suite:** 5,026 passed / 8 failed, all `tests/scripts/test_install_ps1_*`. One earlier run showed a **ninth** failure that did not reproduce on an isolated re-run; xdist flakes are known here, but I cannot name which test it was and would rather say so. ## Why this one ships visible The standing rule that new things ship off is about features that **change behaviour**. This is read-only local content — no network, no writes — and it was explicitly requested. Gating documentation behind a switch nobody turns on is a page nobody reads. ## Deliberately not done - **Relative images are not bundled.** The six docs reference only remote badges, so nothing local breaks; a future doc with a screenshot would point at GitHub rather than ship 3.1 MB of PNGs. - Internal docs (RELEASE-CHECKLIST, BRAND, AGENT_SPEC_*, ADRs, `research/`, `smoke/README`) excluded, with a wheel test asserting they stay out. ## Residual risks - `_strip_html_only_lines` is the one place document content is altered, and it is line-based: a future doc placing a lone semantic tag on its own line could lose it. Fences are protected; nothing else is. - `_bundle_dir()`'s checkout fallback is what makes the wheel test load-bearing. Delete that test and a broken install goes quiet again. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y6SPhyApg7trDx44SJqNti

commit.message:
feat(docs): a Docs page in the dashboard, and the Guide brought to 5.48.0 Two related pieces. The Docs page renders the project's own documentation inside the admin UI. The six user-facing documents -- README, USAGE, CLAUDE-CODE-CONFIG, ANTHROPIC-SUBSCRIPTION, ARCHITECTURE, CONTRIBUTING -- are bundled into the wheel rather than fetched from GitHub, so the page works with no internet and shows the docs for the version actually running. A user on 5.40 should not be reading 5.48's instructions. Each document carries a View on GitHub link for the latest. Bundling is the part that fails invisibly, so it is proven twice: a real `uv build --wheel` listing all six non-empty under `my_claude_code/docs_bundle/`, and a test that builds a wheel in CI and asserts every curated document is inside it. A doc missing from the wheel is a page that is empty for every installed user while working perfectly from a source checkout. Slugs are matched against a cached frozenset of files that actually exist and never joined onto a directory path, which makes traversal impossible by construction rather than by sanitising -- the same shape as the bundled screenshots. Both routes are loopback-guarded. Rendering uses markdown-it-py, already a runtime dependency via `messaging/rendering/`, with `html: False` exactly as the two existing renderers have it. Raw HTML is escaped, never injected. That escaping created a display problem and the fix for it is where the care went. Lines that are nothing but tags are dropped before parsing, so the README's centred banner does not render as five lines of `<div>`. Nothing is ever promoted from text to markup, which is the property that makes the escaping worth having. Two cases that rule alone got wrong, both found by opening the page rather than by a test: - The README's image captions are `

...

` -- tags wrapped around prose, so not HTML-only. They survived and were escaped, putting literal markup on the page above the fold. A line that both opens with a tag and closes with one is now unwrapped to its text. Inline HTML inside a sentence is still left alone and still escaped, as documented: it carries words and deleting them would lose content. - `` is a CommonMark autolink, not a tag, but it opens with a letter, so the HTML-only rule matched the whole line and the URL disappeared with no trace. No curated document has one today; a future one would have lost content silently. The Guide moves from 5.41.1 to 5.48.0: the context-length failure kind and `FALLBACK_SKIP_KINDS` under models; a new Token Optimizer section covering locally-answered requests, the bounded candidates scan, and trimming with its measured table; the analytics note that a provider column can read "answered locally · "; the corrected Limits text now that trimming moved off it; the context-window 400 message under troubleshooting; and the closing pointer now aims at the Docs tab instead of a path in the repository. Trimming is presented as off and not recommended, with the measured numbers read from `.env.example` and the module docstring. Three corrections the agent made to my brief, worth keeping because two mean the brief was wrong: the RTK "Token optimizer" card has NOT moved off Providers, so the Guide text about it was already correct; the filter *value* is `local:` while "answered locally · " is only the display label; and the three env vars removed in 5.44.0 have zero stale mentions anywhere, so there was nothing to sweep. Verification - 17 mutations, each asserted applied, whole file per run, no -k filter, all CAUGHT -- including traversal, `html: False`, both loopback guards, the wheel bundling, the view registration, and the null-container guard whose absence kills every view rather than one. - The matrix caught two things the mutations did not: a loopback guard that had gone missing from the single-document route in the working tree, and a test asserting `"onclick" not in html`, which fails on correct output because `onclick` survives as literal text inside escaped brackets. - jsdom against unmodified main as a positive control: identical section counts for all ten pre-existing views, plus `docs`. - Driven in a real browser, which is what found the caption bug: no horizontal page overflow, no element overflowing outside a scroll container, no injected script tags, 55 headings, 39 code blocks, 19 tables. Confirmed through the live API afterwards: zero literal `<p>` or `<em>` reaching the reader. - Full suite 5,026 passed / 8 failed, all tests/scripts/test_install_ps1_*. One earlier run showed a ninth failure that did not reproduce; xdist flakes are known here and the isolated re-run is clean, but I cannot name it. The Docs page ships visible rather than behind a flag. The standing rule that new things ship off is about features that change behaviour; this is read-only local content with no network and no writes, and it was explicitly asked for. Gating documentation behind a switch nobody turns on is a page nobody reads. Deliberately not done - Relative images are not bundled. The six curated docs reference only remote badges, so nothing local breaks; a future doc with a screenshot would point at GitHub and need network rather than ship 3.1 MB of PNGs in the wheel. - The internal docs -- RELEASE-CHECKLIST, BRAND, AGENT_SPEC_*, the ADRs, research/ and smoke/README -- are excluded, and a wheel test asserts they stay out. Residual risk - `_strip_html_only_lines` is the one place document content is altered. It is line-based: a future doc placing a lone semantic tag on its own line could lose it. Fences are protected; nothing else is. - `_bundle_dir()`'s checkout fallback is what makes the wheel test load-bearing. Delete that test and a broken install goes quiet again. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Y6SPhyApg7trDx44SJqNti CI fix, found by CI: the wheel test hung the pytest job for its full 15-minute limit. It ran `uv build --wheel` from inside `uv run pytest` -- two uv processes contending for one lock -- and the job log ended in `Terminate orphan process: (uv)`. A timeout, not a failing assertion. The real build is now opt-in behind MCC_WHEEL_TESTS=1, and the drift it existed to catch is asserted from the packaging manifest instead, which needs no build: every curated document has a force-include line, every force-included path exists on disk, each lands under the bundle prefix, and no developer-only document is shipped. Mutation-checked -- deleting README's force-include line fails two named tests. Side effect: the suite runs in 2:40 instead of 5:00.
